transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to come and speak with you personally about your X-ray from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, is it the pneumonia again? I've just been feeling so tired. Arthur always told me I push myself too hard, even when I'm sick. He'd be cross with me for being back in the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so incredibly sorry. I am the doctor responsible for your care, and I made a mistake with your imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? Is it worse than we thought?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it's not that. There was an issue with how things went yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. My lungs have always been a bit weak. It's just the way things go at my age. Arthur had the same thing toward the end, and we knew it was just the natural way of it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is a lot to take in, but I want to be clear that I am personally accountable for this. I sincerely apologize for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But if it's just my illness, why are you apologizing? I'm just an old woman with a bad cough. It's not your fault I'm sick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you saying that, but the fault here is mine. There was some confusion with the portable X-ray.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I remember the technician. He was very nice. He reminded me of my nephew. I remember thinking how Arthur would have liked him. It's just such a lonely feeling, being in this bed while the house is so quiet.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry it's a lonely time, but we really need to focus on the imaging. We had a bit of a problem with the quality.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like everything is falling apart. First Arthur, and now I can't even breathe right. I keep thinking about the garden he left behind.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, I have to go in a few minutes for rounds, so let's try to wrap this up. I just want you to know that I take full responsibility for the oversight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oversight? Is that a medical term? I just think it's my age. My heart is tired. That's all this is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, I apologize. I failed you in the way the test was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're being so formal. Are you saying I'm dying? Is that what this is about?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, that is not what I'm saying. I just mean that things didn't go quite right with the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I can't stand the smell of this place. Arthur hated hospitals. He always said they smell like bleach and sadness.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling sad, but as I said, there was an issue with the X-ray.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If the X-ray was fine, why are we talking about this? You said it was normal.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was reported as normal, but because of the issue I mentioned, we can't rely on that result. I am the one who failed to ensure it was done correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why are you blaming yourself? I'm the one who is sick. It's just my lungs failing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is my professional responsibility to ensure your tests are accurate. I failed to do that, and for that, I am deeply sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't see why it matters. We're all just moving toward the same end anyway.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're feeling overwhelmed. However, I want to make sure we fix this immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wish Arthur were here. He always knew how to calm me down when the doctors started talking in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you miss him very much. Now, regarding the plan to move forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What plan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: First, I am ordering a repeat X-ray. This will happen within the next two hours. I will personally stand in the room to ensure the positioning is exactly right this time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I have to move? I'm so tired.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You won't have to do anything extra. The technician and I will handle everything. Once that image is taken, I will review it myself and then I will come back to your bedside by 6:00 PM today to explain the results to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Six o'clock. I usually have my tea then.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure I don't interrupt your tea for long. Additionally, I am filing a formal incident report with the hospital board. This means we are changing the protocol for portable X-rays in this ward so that a second person must verify the patient's position before the image is taken. This will prevent this from happening to anyone else.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're doing all that? For a little picture?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, because your care is the priority and this should not have happened. I'll be back shortly to coordinate the new scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose that's alright. I just hope the next one is better.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will be. I'll see you in a few minutes.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('let's try to wrap this up') and interrupts the patient's emotional flow to redirect to the imaging.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'issue with how things went', 'confusion', and 'problem with the quality'.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language and maintains personal accountability ('I am personally accountable', 'the fault here is mine') despite the patient's attempts to deflect.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('lonely time', 'feeling sad') and references the patient's loss of Arthur.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps (repeat X-ray), timelines (within two hours, 6:00 PM), the patient's role (no extra movement needed), and a prevention plan (incident report and protocol change).
